newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Prodi says Italy, Hungary should expand trade.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy, Hungary should expand trade.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Wednesday that trade links between Hungary and Italy had grown substantially and urged more medium-sized Italian companies to enter the market.

"It's a great honour that the business people could negotiate in the presence of the two prime ministers, the leaders of the Hungarian government and the head of the national bank to talk about how to develop Hungarian-Italian relations," Prodi said in Budapest during a breakfast for business and government leaders.
Prodi, on the second day of a two-day visit, said that "Hungarian-Italian relations are very good and they are no longer based just on trade links -- our investments are significant.

"But there are no such relations which cannot be improved upon and therefore I am especially pleased that not only the big enterprises but also the medium-scale companies are represented here," he added.
"We feel that these relations can be improved by the Italian medium-sized companies, first of all from northern Italy, doing business in Hungary.
"The necessary institutional and financial conditions already exist and I would ask that Italian investors become even more active (in Hungary)," he said.
Italian-Hungarian trade has grown substantially in recent years, to $2.37 billion dollars in 1996 from $1.47 billion in 1993.
In 1996, Hungarian exports to Italy totalled $1.05 billion while imports were $1.31 billion.
